html:
SMTO-TSK-0021 — SMTO couldn't apply this change to your conversations

GUID: c35a77bb-385b-4f56-8026-550bf84d6cf7
Slug: conversation-edit-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The rename, pin or selection you sent wasn't in a form SMTO accepts. For example, the new name was blank or too long. Your conversations weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were renaming, choose Rename again and type a name that isn't blank and is no longer than 160 characters. Conversation names must have some text and stay within 160 characters.
  2. If you were selecting several conversations or scheduled tasks, select Cancel selection, then pick them again with Select, Select all shown or Select all matching. Starting the selection over makes sure it uses one way of choosing conversations, which SMTO needs.
  3. If it still fails, reload the SMTO page and repeat the change. An out-of-date page can send a selection SMTO no longer accepts.

What success looks like

  • The new name or pin shows in the Conversations pane, or the selected count matches what you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If a script made this change, tell them it sent an empty change or mixed both ways of selecting conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A conversation metadata patch or bulk selection was invalid: no non-null title or pinned value was supplied, the title was empty or longer than 160 characters, or the selection mixed explicit conversation IDs with all-matching filters or exclusions.

What this means

  • Metadata patches lack supported non-null fields or valid title bounds, or conversation/schedule selection mixes explicit IDs with all-matching filters/exclusions. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Metadata patches lack supported non-null fields or valid title bounds, or conversation/schedule selection mixes explicit IDs with all-matching filters/exclusions.

How to diagnose it

  • Check patch fields and choose one selection mode; filter/exclusion rules belong only to all-matching selection.

How to fix it

  • Send a metadata patch with a non-null title (1 to 160 characters after trimming) or pinned value. For bulk conversation or schedule actions, send exactly one selection mode: explicit conversation_ids (up to 1,000) or all_matching=true with its query, filters and excluded_ids, never both and never neither.
  • Supply supported metadata or one valid selection mode; keep filters and exclusions with all-matching selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid bounded edit addresses one explicit, reviewable selection.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
